Eliphaz's Third Speech Eliphaz's response to Job's complaint about the prosperity and complacency of the wicked is to put aside his former indirectness and accuse him of a list of specific crimes. He then tempers his attack by setting forth a rosy fantasy of the future that awaits Job if he changes his behavior and attitude.
